newsitem.title: USA: Asarco sees zinc ahead of fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Asarco sees zinc ahead of fundamentals.

text.p: The zinc market has gotten ahead of its fundamentals, Asarco Inc chief executive Richard Osborne said Friday.

Speaking with reporters following the company's quarterly analysts' meeting, he said zinc "is in very substantial deficit, supply versus demand," noting prices remain relatively high despite a recent decline.
Osborne said the supply deficit "will be filled by the restart of the Faro mine."
Anvil Range Mining Corp recently completed financing for a stripping program at the mine, located in Canada's Yukon territory.

The 180,000-tonne-per-year mine -- the third largest zinc mine in North America -- was shut down in December as a result of low zinc prices. The stripping program paves the way for the restart of mining within three to four months.
Since the Faro mine can not ship in the winter, Osborne noted, its zinc will not reach Europe until next summer.
Therefore, he continued, the market will continue to be volitile.
